NEW DELHI: A Kuki woman was killed and another person injured in a gunfight between suspected rival militant groups in Manipur’s Kangpokpi district on Thursday, officials said.The exchange of fire broke out around 11 am in an area between Taphou Kuki village in Kangpokpi district and Kailengjang in neighbouring Senapati district.Following the gunfight, a woman from Taphou Kuki village, who was working in a nearby field, was found shot dead. The victim, identified as Nengboi Chonglo, was reportedly holding a sickle when she was found.Her body was subsequently recovered by local residents and security personnel.The injured person, a man, was rushed to a private hospital in Kangpokpi district.The incident comes days after two Kuki youths, who went missing from the vicinity of Taphou Kuki village on October 28, were found dead in Senapati district on November 1.The killings triggered protests by the Kangpokpi-based Committee on Tribal Unity (COTU), which staged a sit-in demonstration at the district headquarters over what it termed an "unsatisfactory response to the organisation's charter of demands" concerning the abduction and killing of the two youths.COTU has demanded that Taphou Kuki village be brought under the jurisdiction of Kangpokpi district police instead of the Senapati district police station, which currently exercises jurisdiction over the area.According to Manipur Police ADGP (Law and Order) Lhari Dorjee Lhatoo, the state government was considering transferring the case to the National Investigation Agency (NIA)."The Manipur government's proposal to hand over the case to the NIA is at an advanced stage, and necessary orders are awaited," he had said on Tuesday.The ethnic conflict between the Meitei and Kuki communities, which erupted in Manipur in May 2023, continues, having claimed hundreds of lives and displaced thousands of people.
Article Summary: The exchange of fire broke out around 11 am in an area between Taphou Kuki village in Kangpokpi district and Kailengjang in neighbouring Senapati district. Following the gunfight, a woman, who was working in a nearby field, was found shot dead. The victim, identified as Nengboi Chonglo, was reportedly holding a sickle when she was found.

Article Title: 'Sad day for democracy': Bombay HC warns against criminalising constitutional right to protest
Article Text:
Bombay HC said criminal prosecutions should not be initiated to stifle agitations that form part of the democratic process, provided protesters do not resort to violence or damage public or private property.

NEW DELHI: The Bombay high court has quashed an FIR and chargesheet against a man booked for participating in a protest over poor road conditions in Maharashtra 's Chandrapur district, observing that it would be a "sad day for democracy" if criminal prosecutions were used to suppress peaceful agitations. The court said people have a constitutional right to protest as long as they do not resort to violence, take the law into their own hands or damage public or private property.Justice MW Chandwani of the high court's Nagpur bench made the observations in an order passed on October 29. A copy of the order was made available later.The case relates to an agitation held in January this year in Nandgaon village against the poor condition of a road. The protest followed an accident involving a vehicle on the damaged road. Residents had demanded action against the road contractor and officials of the Public Works Department.Nishkarsh Nimgade, a resident of Chandrapur district, was booked for participating in the agitation. The police alleged that the protesters had blocked the road by forming an unlawful assembly.Nimgade subsequently approached the High Court, seeking to quash the FIR and chargesheet filed against him.Allowing his petition, the court said Article 19(1)(b) of the Constitution guarantees citizens the right to assemble peacefully and without arms.It observed that while reasonable restrictions could be imposed on the exercise of this fundamental right, vague charges must not be used to dilute or suppress it."The lines between the constitutional right to protest and the unleashing of penal prosecutions cannot be allowed to be blurred. If this mindset gains traction, it would be a sad day for democracy," the HC remarked.The court further said criminal prosecutions should not be initiated to stifle agitations that form part of the democratic process, provided protesters do not resort to violence or damage public or private property.Describing the prosecution of Nimgade as an abuse of the legal process, the High Court quashed the FIR and chargesheet against him.
Article Summary: Bombay HC said criminal prosecutions should not be initiated to stifle agitations that form part of the democratic process. Court said people have a constitutional right to protest as long as they do not resort to violence, take the law into their own hands or damage public or private property.

NEW DELHI: Security agencies have intensified their manhunt for Mohammad Lateef Bhat, one of four active terrorists featured on a recently released wanted poster by Jammu and Kashmir Police, following his identification as a suspect in Wednesday’s attack on CRPF personnel in Kulgam.Bhat, a resident of Khrewan Chadder in Kulgam, is considered one of the few remaining local terrorists active in the valley. He is affiliated with the Kashmir Revolutionary Army (KRA), a proxy group floated by Pak-based Lashkar-e-Taiba (LeT) to conceal its direct involvement.Operating across South Kashmir, particularly in the Kulgam, Shopian, and Anantnag districts, Bhat is known to exercise influence over local over ground worker (OGW) networks.Investigating agencies suspect Bhat’s involvement in several recent terror strikes in the region. These include the July 22 fatal shooting of J&K Police Head Constable Aashiq Hussain in Anantnag and the July 31 targeted killing of two migrant workers from Chhattisgarh, Deepak and Bhupendra, in Kulgam.Security forces noted that Bhat operates differently from standard modules. “Known to be possessing an AK-47, he executes swift strikes either alone or in small groups before immediately blending into the local population,” said a source.In July 2026, Bhat was trapped alongside top LeT commander Zakir Ganie during a security force siege on a house in Shopian. While Ganie was neutralised in the encounter, Bhat is learnt to have managed to break through the cordon and escape, evading a massive follow-up search operation.While law enforcement agencies state that the other three individuals listed on the wanted poster— Bilal Ahmad Mir, Abid Qayoom Lone, and Mohammad Umar Mir — are currently operating from across the border in Pakistan-occupied Jammu & Kashmir (PoJK), Bhat remains the sole local operative actively grounded in South Kashmir.Authorities had last week issued a public appeal for information on the whereabouts of the four suspects, promising strict confidentiality and a cash reward. Inputs can be shared directly with security agencies through designated helplines, they had said.
Article Summary: Mohammad Lateef Bhat is one of four active terrorists featured on a recently released wanted poster by Jammu and Kashmir Police. Bhat, a resident of Khrewan Chadder in Kulgam, is considered one of the few remaining local terrorists active in the valley. He is affiliated with the Kashmir Revolutionary Army (KRA), a proxy group floated by Pak-based Lashkar-e-Taiba.

Both were part of the Special Operations Group (SOG) of the local police and were posted at Kiyar village in Dachhan.The two SPOs had gone missing on Wednesday while travelling from their camp to an Army post at Dharna-Marwah, officials said.Their service weapons were also missing, raising suspicion of a possible militant angle, they added.According to officials, the two personnel had left for patrol duty earlier in the day. NEW DELHI: National Conference president Farooq Abdullah on Thursday advocated dialogue between India and Pakistan , saying meaningful engagement between New Delhi and Islamabad must begin without waiting for hostilities to end.Talking to reporters, Abdullah asserted that bullets and military confrontation cannot resolve political disputes."Ab aap intezaar karenge, jab tak aap sabki goliyan band ho jayengi, tab tak raat ho jayegi (If you keep waiting for everyone to stop firing, it will be too late by the time the guns fall silent)," Abdullah said."I have always told Pakistan to stop terrorism. Nothing can be achieved through terrorism. The process of dialogue must begin because only through talks can a way forward be found," he added.The former Jammu and Kashmir chief minister also called for the revival of SAARC, saying regional countries must come together to resolve their differences and work towards collective progress."India is the largest country in the region, and Indira Gandhi had shown the way for India to maintain cordial and sympathetic relations with neighbouring countries.We must revive SAARC so that all of us can sit together, resolve our disputes and work towards progress and development," he said.Reacting to the recent twin terror attacks in Kulgam and Kishtwar districts, which claimed the lives of two Special Police Officers (SPOs) and left three CRPF personnel injured within two days, Abdullah asserted that those harbouring ambitions of taking Kashmir must abandon such notions. He also said that terrorism would never succeed in its designs.However, he expressed concern over claims in Delhi that terrorism had ended in Jammu and Kashmir, maintaining that the recent incidents indicated that the threat persisted and that concrete measures were needed to eliminate it."I have already said such incidents are still happening. One never knows where the next attack might take place," he said.This comes days after Abdullah courted criticism for his remarks that Pakistan's repeated efforts to raise the Kashmir issue internationally were putting pressure on India.He alleged that the Centre's intentions towards Jammu and Kashmir were not good and urged people to stand up for their rights.“What can you expect from Delhi? You must have the courage to stand up to them and fight. If you do not, you will be wiped out. Your name and identity will disappear, and no one will even remember you. Our neighbour (Pakistan) is constantly after them. It goes everywhere, saying that the Kashmir issue has not been resolved.It is protecting us; otherwise, their intentions are not good. They say one thing but do something entirely different,” Abdullah said.He also called on people to stand by the truth, warning that their future would remain insecure unless they spoke out.“You must have the courage to stand by the truth. Speaking the truth is not easy, but unless you speak the truth and stand firm by it, your future will never be secure,” he said.
Article Summary: National Conference president Farooq Abdullah advocates dialogue between India and Pakistan. He says meaningful engagement between New Delhi and Islamabad must begin without waiting for hostilities to end. The former Jammu and Kashmir chief minister also called for the revival of SAARC.

NEW DELHI: Union minister Kiren Rijiju on Tuesday slammed Lok Sabha leader of opposition Rahul Gandhi for attacking Prime Minister Narendra Modi over his remarks on 'Dimagi Naxal'.In a social media post on X, Rijiju reminded Rahul that former Prime Minister Manmohan Singh had described Left-wing extremism as the biggest internal security threat to the country."Rahul ji, thank Modi ji for eliminating the Armed Maoists. Former PM Dr Manmohan Singh ji had famously described Left-Wing Extremism and Naxalism as 'The single biggest internal security threat' to India," Rijiju said."Next target is to finish Dimagi Naxals," he added.This comes a day after Rahul hit back at PM Modi over his 'Dimagi Naxal' remarks, claiming that the CRPF jawans' facial expressions suggested they did not believe the Prime Minister's claims.In a post on X addressed to CRPF personnel who attended PM Modi's Diwali event in Bastar, Rahul said, "Your faces said it all: you didn't buy the PM's lies. He called us Naxals.""My challenge stands. Let him debate me on who is anti-national and who is controlled by foreign forces. Any time, any place," he said, adding, "My guarantee: after the debate, the PM won't have the guts to stand in front of a single jawan again."The war of words began after PM Modi, while celebrating Diwali with security personnel in Bastar, Chhattisgarh, said that although armed Naxalites had been wiped out from forests, "Dimagi Naxals" had infiltrated several organisations and political parties and were inciting people against the Constitution and democracy.The Prime Minister also accused previous governments of restricting the freedom of security personnel engaged in anti-Naxal operations, saying his government had given them the authority to take necessary decisions."We must remember one thing. Naxalites have been eliminated, but the threat is not yet over. While armed Naxalites have been wiped out from the forests, 'Dimagi Naxals' have taken control of several organisations. Even today, they are inciting people against the country's Constitution and democracy. These 'Dimagi Naxals' have also infiltrated several political parties and different organisations. We must identify them, defeat them and ensure the security of the nation," PM Modi said.The remarks came months after the Centre announced on March 31 that the country had been freed from the menace of Naxalism, following the elimination of several Maoist leaders and cadres and the surrender of hundreds of others.
Article Summary: Rijiju reminded Rahul that former PM Manmohan Singh had described Left-wing extremism as the biggest internal security threat to the country. LUCKNOW: Chief minister Yogi Adityanath on Wednesday defended the bursting of firecrackers during Diwali, saying he had personally participated in celebrations in Ayodhya and arguing that concerns over pollution were being selectively raised.Speaking at an event in Lucknow, Yogi said people were now able to celebrate Diwali and other festivals "without fear" and criticised those who, he claimed, objected to firecrackers.Referring to complaints about air quality, he said pollution may increase during Diwali but would also subside. "Lots of people said there was pollution due to Diwali celebrations. I said pollution did happen but it will end also. Why worry about it?" he said. The chief minister used the remarks to target political opponents, alleging that while corruption had "polluted the entire system," criticism was directed at common people celebrating for a single day. He maintained that any pollution caused by crackers was temporary and not a major issue, adding that it was good people celebrated Diwali with "dhoom dharaka." He said he was happy that large numbers of people lit firecrackers.Yogi reiterated his govt's stance of imposing no restrictions on Diwali celebrations and said he was in Ayodhya during the lighting of firecrackers. He also said that festivals had been celebrated with grandeur this year. Contrasting the present with the period before 2017, the chief minister claimed festivals were earlier preceded by riots and curfews, which affected markets and public safety. He said that over the past 9.5 years there had been no curfews and no "danga," adding that the situation in Uttar Pradesh had changed.
Article Summary: Chief minister Yogi Adityanath on Wednesday defended the bursting of firecrackers during Diwali. NEW DELHI: Two Special Police Officers (SPOs) went missing from Jammu and Kashmir 's Kishtwar district on Wednesday, prompting a search operation, officials said, according to news agency PTI.Both officers were part of the Special Operations Group (SOG) deployed in the Kiyar area of Dachhan in Kishtwar.According to reports, the two SPOs had left for patrol duty earlier in the day. Police teams have launched a search operation to trace them, officials said, PTI reported.The incident comes amid a separate attack on security personnel in Kulgam district, where three Central Reserve Police Force ( CRPF ) personnel were injured after unidentified motorcycle-borne assailants opened fire at a security checkpoint on Wednesday afternoon.The firing took place at around 2.15 pm when the assailants targeted CRPF personnel deployed at a naka, or security checkpoint, in Kulgam, the force said. The attackers fled shortly after opening fire."There has been firing on CRPF Naka at Kulgam, Kashmir. Three personnel injured. Operations are going on to nab the perpetrators and best possible treatment is being provided to the injured personnel," the CRPF said in a statement.The injured personnel were shifted to Government Medical College (GMC), Anantnag, for treatment. Security agencies have launched a search operation to track down the attackers, an official said.The checkpoint is around 4 km from the National Highway. Of the three injured personnel, two sustained minor injuries, while the third was reported to be slightly serious, the official said, ANI reported.The injured CRPF personnel have been identified as Head Constable Somveer Singh and Constables Rakesh Dass and Santosh Chandru. Chandru, a resident of West Bengal, sustained injuries to his abdomen and spine. His condition was stated to be slightly serious.Dass, who hails from Assam, suffered a bullet injury to his leg, while Singh, a resident of Madhya Pradesh, sustained a bullet injury to his arm. SRINAGAR: As Ladakh’s administration Wednesday imposed a complete ban on protests and demonstrations within the municipal limits of Leh and Kargil, citing the municipal and hill council polls scheduled for Nov 23 and Dec 4, respectively, Ladakhi leaders, including Leh Apex Body (LAB) member and climate activist Sonam Wangchuk , appealed to President Droupadi Murmu, Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Union home minister Amit Shah to intervene to defer the polls, citing harsh winter conditions and the likely exclusion of a large section of the electorate.“It is an SOS call from Ladakh to the President, the Prime Minister and the Union home minister. We are sending this message to the people of India also,” the joint appeal said.Earlier in the day, the office of the chief electoral officer issued an order stating that the model code of conduct has been enforced and will remain in force till the completion of the election process. The order said organising of political dharnas, protests, demonstrations, sit-ins, rallies or similar collective activities within the municipal limits of Leh and Kargil during the currency of the model code of conduct has the potential to intimidate voters, disturb public order, and vitiate the atmosphere for free and fair electionsFlanked by Ladakh MP Mohmad Haneefa, LAB co-chairman Chering Dorjay Lakrook and Kargil Democratic Alliance (KDA) co-chairmen Asgar Ali Karbali and Sajjad Kargili, Wangchuk said the administration was forcing elections on people during the harsh winter, when temperatures in some parts of Ladakh fall below minus 30°C. “Ladakh is known as the world’s coldest inhabited place. The weather forecast for Dec indicates snowfall. How will elections be conducted in such conditions? Half of the population is outside Ladakh, while students are already studying in different cities. When Leh, Kargil and other areas are nearly empty, why are you holding elections?” he asked.“Indian democracy has a great tradition in Ladakh. Earlier, even two voters in Demchok were facilitated through helicopters to ensure their participation.So why is the administration ignoring half of the population now,” Wangchuk said. He appealed to the country’s leadership, including the opposition and people across India, to pay attention to Ladakh and oppose what he termed an arbitrary decision by the lieutenant-governor’s administration.Haneefa said he had met the Ladakh L-G and told him holding elections during winter would deprive a large number of people of their right to vote. He said despite it they issued the poll notification.Lakrook said holding elections during peak winter was unheard of in Ladakh. He said May or June would be more suitable time ensure maximum voter participation. Karbali accused the L-G of imposing its decisions on Ladakh’s people. He said the region has traditionally recorded around 90% voter turnout but the administration was scheduling elections at a time when nearly 30% of the population would be outside the Union Territory.Kargili alleged that the administration was making every effort to defame LAB and KDA and that holding elections in Dec was an infringement of people’s voting rights and a denial of adequate political representation.
Article Summary: Ladakh’s administration Wednesday imposed a complete ban on protests and demonstrations within the municipal limits of Leh and Kargil. Ladakhi leaders appealed to President Droupadi Murmu, Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Union home minister Amit Shah to intervene to defer the polls.

Article Title: National Conference's twin troubles: Can Farooq Abdullah contain brewing revolt against Omar?
Article Text:
The Abdullahs are facing the challenge of keeping the National Conference united amid mounting dissent.

The show of unity

Farooq Abdullah dismisses reports of a split within the National Conference, asserting that the party remains united despite growing internal discontent.

The ideological rupture: Ruhullah's 'decree of freedom'

Aga Syed Ruhullah Mehdi accused the NC leadership of abandoning its promises on Kashmir's dignity and autonomy after the abrogation of Article 370.

The arithmetic ceiling

Omar Abdullah's Union Territory dilemma

CM Abdullah on statehood resolution.

Political space opening up beyond NC

NEW DELHI: Two years after sweeping to power on a promise to reclaim Jammu and Kashmir ’s political identity and dignity, Omar Abdullah ’s government is confronting the limits of governing a Union Territory with constrained powers.What began as a historic return to power in October 2024 has increasingly turned into a political and administrative tightrope. While 89-year-old National Conference patron Farooq Abdullah has stepped in to contain simmering discontent among MLAs left out of the cabinet expansion, an ideological rupture has emerged with the exit of Srinagar MP Aga Syed Ruhullah Mehdi, who has accused the party leadership of abandoning its core promises.Caught between disgruntled legislators seeking a greater share in government and a prominent party voice questioning its political compromises, the National Conference faces a twin challenge. The party has accused the BJP of exploiting its internal divisions to engineer an ' Operation Lotus ' in Jammu and Kashmir. But is this an opposition attempt to destabilise the government, or does the turmoil point to a leadership crisis under Omar Abdullah?The gates of the Abdullahs' Gupkar residence in Srinagar opened to a familiar political spectacle last week as yet another party leadership put up a show of strength amid growing discontent within its ranks.Standing alongside 15 MLAs unhappy with the recent cabinet expansion, 89-year-old National Conference (NC) president Farooq Abdullah sought to project an image of an organisation firmly in control of its affairs."The baseless reports being spread that the National Conference is divided are completely false. This organisation is united, and those who think they can break this organisation should understand that it has never been broken and will never be broken," Farooq declared.He acknowledged that the legislators had genuine grievances and promised that some concerns would be addressed immediately, while others would be taken up gradually.But behind the show of unity, there's a bigger contradiction confronting Jammu and Kashmir chief minister Omar Abdullah. The National Conference, which swept the 2024 assembly elections on the promise of reclaiming Kashmir's political identity, dignity and special status, is caught between the compromises of governing a Union Territory and the expectations of the constituency that brought it to power.The party is facing two distinct challenges. While a section of its MLAs is demanding a greater share in the government and a say in decision-making, one of its most prominent political voices, Srinagar MP Aga Syed Ruhullah Mehdi, has walked out accusing the leadership of abandoning the very promises on which it sought votes.The fragility of the NC's united front was exposed three days before Farooq met with the disgruntled legislators.On November 3, at a gathering in Behisht-e-Zehra Park in Budgam marking the 26th death anniversary of his assassinated father, Aga Syed Mehdi, Ruhullah announced his resignation from both the National Conference and the Lok Sabha.In an 80-minute address, the Srinagar MP launched a scathing attack on Farooq and Omar Abdullah, accusing the leadership of abandoning its promises on Article 370 , political prisoners and public relief.Describing his departure as a "decree of freedom", Ruhullah called the NC a "deceitful, corrupt organisation"."You told people that you were the guardians of their dignity. You said that if anyone touched that dignity, it would be like grabbing you by the collar. That dignity was buried on August 5, 2019. Tell me now, where is that dignity? Where is that autonomy?" he asked, targeting the party leadership.He accused the NC of seeking power on promises it had failed to fulfil and said he could no longer lend his name to what he described as political humiliation.On November 6, Lok Sabha Speaker Om Birla formally accepted his resignation, creating a vacancy in the Srinagar parliamentary constituency.Ruhullah's departure is more than an organisational setback for the NC. Elected to the Lok Sabha on the party's ticket in 2024, he had emerged as one of its most vocal faces on the question of Kashmir's political rights after the abrogation of Article 370 in August 2019.While Omar Abdullah has sought to pursue the restoration of statehood and special status through legislative and political channels, Ruhullah has demanded a more uncompromising approach. His exit gives him the opportunity to position himself as a voice of those who believe the NC has softened its stand after coming to power.He has hinted at launching a broader political movement rather than immediately forming a new party, saying he wants to bring together people committed to restoring the dignity and rights of Jammu and Kashmir.The NC, meanwhile, has questioned his own record, asking why he did not move a resolution or private member's bill in Parliament on special status or mobilise fellow MPs on the issue, despite having secured the support of more than 100 parliamentarians for an impeachment motion against an Allahabad High Court judge.The public exchange has exposed a larger ideological fault line: can the NC continue to claim ownership of the political struggle for Kashmir's rights while defending its record in government?While the ideological dissent has played out in public, the discontent within the legislative wing has centred on the distribution of power.The immediate trigger was the October 27 cabinet expansion, in which four new ministers were inducted, taking the council of ministers to its maximum permissible strength of nine.The restriction is rooted in Section 53 of the Jammu and Kashmir Reorganisation Act, 2019, which caps the council of ministers at 10% of the total membership of the Legislative Assembly. With 90 elected seats, the permissible strength is nine, including the chief minister.This creates a structural constraint for Omar Abdullah. Unlike a full-fledged state, where the constitutional ceiling for the council of ministers is 15% of the assembly's strength, Jammu and Kashmir's Union Territory framework leaves the CM with a smaller pool of ministerial positions to distribute.With all nine positions occupied, accommodating more aspirants would require dropping or replacing existing ministers.Several senior legislators, including six-time MLA Mubarak Gul, were reportedly unhappy at being left out. The discontent was not limited to ministerial berths. The legislators also raised concerns about administrative functioning, organisational decisions and what they described as the concentration of authority among a small group of leaders and advisers.A group of 18 aggrieved legislators had met a week before the Friday meeting. The subsequent gathering of 15 MLAs at Gupkar brought their grievances directly to Farooq and Omar Abdullah.The legislators reportedly sought a review of the cabinet, changes in the functioning of the CM's office and a mechanism to ensure that elected representatives have a greater say in government decisions.One of the legislators, Nazir Gurezi, sought to play down speculation about the emergence of a separate faction."A few days ago, we sat together at a place, and from there, social media hyped it up as if a separate faction had emerged from the National Conference. No separate faction or party has emerged," he said.Gurezi added that the legislators had placed their concerns before the CM and the party president, who had assured them that the issues would be addressed.For Omar Abdullah, however, the problem is not merely placating a group of unhappy MLAs. The cabinet expansion has exhausted the government's primary instrument of political accommodation. Any reshuffle could create fresh resentment among those who have already secured ministerial positions.Farooq's intervention may have prevented the discontent from turning into an open confrontation for now, but the leadership will have to find ways of accommodating senior legislators without triggering another round of dissatisfaction.The constraints facing Omar Abdullah go beyond cabinet arithmetic. They strike at the heart of the political contradiction of running an elected government in a Union Territory where the Lieutenant Governor and the Centre retain significant powers.Omar has repeatedly complained about the limits placed on his government, particularly in matters involving administration and the functioning of the bureaucracy.During the September 2026 assembly proceedings on a resolution seeking immediate restoration of full statehood, he revealed that the Law Secretary had written to the Speaker questioning whether the resolution should be discussed because the matter was sub judice. The chief secretary had also written to the Speaker.Omar, who also holds the law portfolio, expressed surprise at the communications."I am a law minister and I don't know that my law secretary is giving you an opinion. As a CM I don't know the chief secretary is writing to the Speaker against my resolution. I don't know on whose behalf it is being done," he said.He went on to question whether such a situation would arise in a full-fledged state."Would you think such a thing would happen in any State? This happens only in UT where a CM moves a resolution and the law secretary gives an opinion against it," he said.The episode illustrates the difficult position in which the chief minister finds himself. To deliver on everyday governance, including infrastructure, electricity, welfare schemes and administrative decisions, Omar has to work within the existing institutional arrangement. But the same arrangement limits his authority and has become a source of political frustration for his government.Every compromise with the Centre risks being interpreted by sections of the electorate as a dilution of the NC's political promises. Every confrontation, meanwhile, can further constrain the government's ability to function.The NC's August 19, 2024 manifesto had made restoration of Articles 370 and 35A a key promise. It also pledged to work towards restoration of statehood, repeal of the Public Safety Act and release of political prisoners.The party subsequently sought to demonstrate its commitment through the assembly. On November 6, 2024, the House passed a resolution seeking restoration of special status, a move Ruhullah had initially welcomed.But two years after the abrogation of Article 370, the Centre has given no indication of reversing its decision. Statehood, too, remains unresolved, while the reservation policy has become another source of friction between the government and sections of the electorate.The NC has defended its record on reservations, saying its cabinet sub-committee has initiated changes but that the decisions are awaiting action from the Centre and the Lieutenant Governor's administration.Farooq Abdullah, after Friday's meeting, reiterated that the party would continue its fight for statehood and Articles 370 and 35A, taking the struggle to its "logical conclusion".Ruhullah's exit could challenge the NC's claim to represent Kashmir's political aspirations. Having been elected on its ticket in 2024, he may now seek to occupy the political space he believes the party has vacated.The political implications will depend on whether Ruhullah can translate his criticism into an organised platform and attract support beyond his existing constituency. His resignation has already created a vacancy in Srinagar, and the eventual by-election could become an important test of the political space he hopes to occupy.The BJP has been quick to seize on the National Conference's internal troubles. On November 3, BJP national vice president Ram Madhav said Ruhullah's rally in Budgam had the blessings of "our people". The NC subsequently accused the BJP of attempting "Operation Lotus" in Kashmir, a charge the party has denied. For the BJP, the public friction within the ruling party offers an opportunity to question its cohesion and, more importantly, Omar Abdullah's leadership.The Congress, the NC's alliance partner, has taken a more cautious line. It has sought to play down the developments, attributing Ruhullah's departure to ideological differences while expressing confidence that the NC would resolve its internal disagreements.But the strains within its ally also pose a political concern for the Congress, given its investment in the governing arrangement.For the Abdullahs, however, the challenge is that the two crises have unfolded back-to-back on different fronts.Farooq Abdullah's show of unity at Gupkar may have helped contain the immediate optics of the MLAs' rebellion. It does little, however, to answer the larger questions raised by Ruhullah's exit.The next few months will answer whether Omar Abdullah can hold his flock together and retain the public's trust at the same time.
Article Summary: The National Conference is caught between the compromises of governing a Union Territory and the expectations of the constituency that brought it to power. The party is facing two distinct challenges. A section of its MLAs is demanding a greater share in the government and a say in decision-making. Srinagar MP Aga Syed Ruhullah Mehdi has walked out accusing the leadership of abandoning the very promises on which it sought votes.

Article Title: 3 CRPF men wounded as terrorists strike patrol in south Kashmir
Article Text:
3 CRPF men wounded as terrorists strike patrol in south Kashmir

SRINAGAR: A CRPF head constable and two constables were wounded when terrorists fired at a patrol in south Kashmir’s Akhran area of Kulgam district around 2pm Wednesday, ending a long lull in attacks on security forces in the valley. Constable Santosh Chandru, who suffered bullet wounds to his abdomen and spine, was airlifted to Army’s 92 Base Hospital in Srinagar in a critical condition. Constable Rakesh Dass and head constable Somveer Singh were stable.The attack on personnel of 46 CRPF battalion was the third major terrorist strike in Kashmir this year, but the first targeting security forces in a long time. The attackers escaped after the shooting.CCTV footage showed a CRPF trooper running for cover as gunfire erupted near a row of closed shops around 2.06pm. A colleague appeared from the left and moved towards the direction of gunfire. The first returned with his weapon and joined him. Another trooper in full combat gear was seen climbing onto a rooftop around 2.07pm. A minute later, a voice, apparently that of a wounded man outside the frame, could be heard saying: “Hamein goli lagi hai” (I am hit).A CRPF officer said the footage appeared genuine and was being examined. The attackers allegedly used a high-calibre weapon, possibly an AK-47. “It doesn’t look like pistol fire,” he said, declining to confirm whether they were riding a motorcycle.Army, CRPF and J&K police sealed the area and launched a manhunt. Security was heightened across Kashmir. Police described the strike as a sign of terrorists’ “growing frustration and desperation” in the face of heightened security alertness and area domination, and praised the personnel’s response.The attack happened while lieutenant governor Manoj Sinha was in Kulgam, attending a festival at Degree College, far from the site. CPM MLA MY Tarigami from Kulgam, who was with Sinha, said they learnt about the attack as the programme was drawing to a close. “We were celebrating our cultural heritage. There were poets and writers present and this happened. It is highly unfortunate,” he said, condemning terrorism.The strike came after Kashmir range IG Sujit Kumar said on Oct 5 that only one Kashmiri terrorist remained active in the valley, backed by a few foreign terrorists. Police identified him as Mohammad Lateef Bhat of Kulgam.
Article Summary: A CRPF head constable and two constables were wounded when terrorists fired at a patrol in south Kashmir. Constable Santosh Chandru was airlifted to Army’s 92 Base Hospital in Srinagar in a critical condition. The attack on personnel of 46 CRPF battalion was the third major terrorist strike in Kashmir this year.

Article Title: 'Congress leaders in Punjab must break silence': Sukhbir Badal on Sonia Gandhi's 'clean chit' to 'killers of Sikhs'
Article Text:
Sukhbir Badal on Sonia Gandhi's memoir

NEW DELHI: Shiromani Akali Dal (SAD) president Sukhbir Singh Badal on Wednesday criticised the Congress over Sonia Gandhi ’s remarks on Operation Blue Star , saying that she had given a “clean chit” to "the killers of thousands of innocent Sikhs."“Congress leaders in Punjab must break their silence over Sonia Gandhi’s clean chit to those responsible for the killing of thousands of innocent Sikhs in 1984,” the former Punjab deputy chief minister said in a post on X.Badal also claimed that Sonia Gandhi’s memoir, "Belonging: A Journey of Love," released in India on Tuesday, contained an “admission” that her husband, then Prime Minister Rajiv Gandhi, had “purposely and personally” decided against deploying Army units in Delhi to protect the Sikh community.“This finally provides the clinching evidence of the Congress government’s patronage of the anti-Sikh massacre. The Congress government could send a Sikh general to lead Operation Blue Star at Sachkhand Sri Harmandir Sahib and Sri Akal Takht Sahib, but would not deploy Sikh Army personnel to protect innocent Sikhs in 1984?” he asked.The SAD chief was referring to retired lieutenant general Kuldeep Singh Brar, who commanded the Army's Operation Blue Star at the Golden Temple in Amritsar, Punjab.Badal further asked whether Punjab Congress leaders "endorse" Rajiv Gandhi's decision not to deploy the Army in Delhi."Do Punjab Congress leaders, including Sikh leaders, endorse this decision to leave innocent Sikhs at the mercy of marauding killers belonging to the Congress party and the government headed by Rajiv Gandhi? Will they ask Sonia Gandhi to explain why Rajiv Gandhi chose to stop the army deployment to save the lives of innocent Sikhs? Cowardly silence won’t do," he added.Anti-Sikh violence erupted across the country, particularly in Delhi, following the assassination of then Prime Minister Indira Gandhi by her Sikh bodyguards on October 31, 1984. The assassination came months after Operation Blue Star at the Golden Temple in June 1984. Indira Gandhi was succeeded as Prime Minister by her son, Rajiv Gandhi.In her memoir, Sonia Gandhi writes that her mother-in-law, Indira Gandhi, was “left with no choice” and “reluctantly” ordered the armed forces to launch Operation Blue Star.“Then intelligence reports informed Mrs Gandhi that the declaration of Khalistan as an independent state was imminent: Bhindranwale and his cohort planned to announce it and hoist its flag on the Har Mandir Sahib, the Golden Temple, on India's Independence Day, August 15,” she wrote.The former Congress president was referring to Jarnail Singh Bhindranwale, who led the movement for a separate Sikh homeland of Khalistan. Bhindranwale and his supporters had been based inside the Golden Temple complex since 1982."Indira Gandhi's own relationship with the Sikh community was a deep and strong one, but the problem was spiralling; she held meetings until late hours of the night, hardly ate her meals and looked disturbed for days ... A week or so later, an intelligence official brought to Mrs Gandhi a film with harrowing visuals of the aftermath: As my mother-in-law watched the slow-moving record, I could see her face wet with tears -- tears of pain and regret, I think: sorrow at the manner which the siege had ended, at the large number of lives lost. "Sonia Gandhi further wrote that Indira Gandhi had “flatly refused” to remove her Sikh bodyguards, a decision for which she ultimately “paid” with her life when two of them opened fire on her.
Article Summary: Sukhbir Singh Badal criticises Congress over Sonia Gandhi’s remarks on Operation Blue Star. Badal says Sonia Gandhi had given a “clean chit” to “the killers of thousands of innocent Sikhs’

BSF recovers DJI drone near International Border in Samba

NEW DELHI: A suspected Pakistani drone was recovered from an agricultural field near the International Border in Jammu and Kashmir 's Samba district on Thursday, officials told news agency PTI.The drone, identified as a DJI Matrice 300 RTK, was found near Border Outpost Lalfamkima, around 800 metres from the International Border, during a search operation launched by the Border Security Force (BSF).No payload was found attached to the drone at the time of its recovery, officials told PTI.The drone has been sent to the Forensic Science Laboratory (FSL) for a detailed examination.Investigators are expected to analyse the device to establish its technical details and gather information about its origin, ownership and possible flight history.According to officials, the BSF launched the search operation after troops spotted suspected drone movement from across the border in the early hours of Thursday.The personnel subsequently activated the anti-drone mechanism before carrying out the search.
Article Summary: The drone, identified as a DJI Matrice 300 RTK, was found near Border Outpost Lalfamkima. No payload was found attached to the drone at the time of its recovery. The drone has been sent to the Forensic Science Laboratory (FSL) for a detailed examination.

Article Title: Geelani’s granddaughter Ruwa Shah likely to join PDP

Geelani’s granddaughter Ruwa Shah likely to join PDP

SRINAGAR: Ruwa Shah, granddaughter of late separatist leader Syed Ali Geelani, is likely to enter mainstream politics and join Mehbooba Mufti-led People’s Democratic Party (PDP), according to sources.A freelance journalist who has been contributing to various national and international publications, Ruwa has not spoken about the possible move, but PDP members said she was welcome to join the party. “It (PDP) is her own home and her own party. The party president considers her like a daughter,” a PDP functionary said.Quoting Mehbooba, another party member said Ruwa could be a valuable contributor to Kashmir if she joined politics, as she “has seen so much and suffered”.Ruwa’s father and Geelani’s son-in-law, Altaf Ahmad Shah alias Fantoosh, was also a separatist who was arrested by the National Investigation Agency in 2018, along with several others, in a terror funding case. He died in AIIMS-Delhi in Oct 2022 while lodged in Tihar Jail. Her pinned tweet of Oct 11, 2022, reads, “After more than five years, my Abbu is back to his home, buried in his ancestral graveyard, next to his father.Ya Allah Shukr.”In Oct 2021, Ruwa’s brother, Anees-ul-Islam, was removed from his position as a research officer at the govt-owned Sher-i-Kashmir International Conference Centre in Srinagar. He had been appointed to the post in 2016, during the PDP-BJP govt headed by Mehbooba.
Article Summary: Ruwa Shah, granddaughter of late separatist leader Syed Ali Geelani, is likely to enter mainstream politics and join People’s Democratic Party. PDP members said she was welcome to join the party. “It (PDP) is her own home and her own party. The party president considers her like a daughter,” a PDP functionary said.

Article Title: Iran unveils underground 'missile city', warns US of strikes across region & beyond
Article Text:
Iran said the underground complex contained several types of ballistic and cruise missiles.

Iran warns US against renewed military action

Iran's big claims on missile production

Trump says Iran's military is effectively over

Iran has released footage of a vast underground military facility displaying ballistic and cruise missiles, as its military leadership warned that American forces across the Middle East and beyond could come under attack if the conflict with the US resumes.The Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) unveiled the facility, which it described as a new underground ‘missile city’, during its Aerospace Week. The footage, released by Iranian state-linked media, showed long rows of missiles and launch systems stored inside tunnels.The unveiling was attended by IRGC Aerospace Force commander Brig Gen Seyyed Majid Mousavi and Armed Forces Chief of Staff Maj Gen Ali Abdollahi. The facility's location, the number of weapons stored there and its operational capabilities have not been independently confirmed.Iran said the underground complex contained several types of ballistic and cruise missiles. Among the weapons shown were the Fattah, which Tehran describes as a hypersonic missile, and the long-range Khorramshahr.Some weapons in the footage were blurred, apparently to conceal details.A portrait of Hassan Tehrani Moghaddam, regarded as the father of Iran's missile programme, was also visible inside the facility, along with images of Mojtaba Khamenei and IRGC flags.Mousavi used the unveiling to issue a warning to Iran's adversaries, saying the country was prepared to respond to threats across the region and beyond."If necessary, we will bring all of their capacities in the region and beyond under our fire, and leave nothing for the enemy but defeat," he said.Abdollahi praised Iran's missile crews and claimed that the US had failed to weaken the country despite deploying large quantities of advanced weapons. He also warned that Iran had more military capabilities to reveal.The announcement came amid similar warnings from Iran's political leadership. Mohsen Rezaei, secretary of the Supreme National Security Council, claimed that the war had already damaged the US government and urged Washington to accept Iran's conditions for ending the conflict.Parliament Speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf accused Israel of trying to draw the US into a prolonged war with Iran. He said the underground facility demonstrated Tehran's ability to develop advanced military technology even while facing attacks.Iran has repeatedly presented its underground military facilities as a way to protect its weapons and production capabilities from air strikes.IRGC spokesman Brig Gen Hossein Mohebbi had earlier said that missile and drone manufacturing lines had been shifted from surface locations to underground complexes. He described them as "missile production cities" rather than simply storage facilities.Mohebbi argued that Iran's domestic expertise, large territory and flexible infrastructure would allow it to continue manufacturing weapons even under heavy bombardment. However, these claims have not been independently verified.The extent of the damage caused by earlier strikes and the number of Iranian missiles and launchers still available remain unclear. While some assessments suggest that a large proportion of underground facilities remain operational, estimates of surviving launch systems vary.The latest unveiling is intended to demonstrate that Iran can preserve its missile capabilities despite sustained military pressure. It also highlights Tehran's strategy of moving weapons and production facilities underground to make them harder to locate and destroy.The unveiling comes as diplomatic efforts to end the conflict continue, with US President Donald Trump striking a more confident tone about the situation."Iran militarily is effectively over," Trump told reporters at the White House after meeting Qatar's prime minister. He also said there was "positive momentum" behind efforts to end the conflict.Renewed American strikes were "highly unlikely", he said, although the US remained "locked and loaded" if circumstances changed.US secretary of state Marco Rubio, meanwhile, said economic pressure was beginning to affect Tehran. He argued that Iran needed money for its nuclear programme and to support groups such as Hamas, Hezbollah and Shia militias.The economic pressure has also affected ordinary Iranians, with rising prices and inflation adding to the difficulties faced by families.Qatar, which has played a mediating role in the crisis, said it was continuing efforts to bring the uncertainty to an end. Foreign Ministry spokesman Ibrahim bin Sultan Al-Hashmi said there were "positive reactions from both sides", but warned that the approaching winter and continued closure of the Strait of Hormuz were increasing the cost of the crisis.
Article Summary: Iran says underground complex contains several types of ballistic and cruise missiles. Among the weapons shown were the Fattah, which Tehran describes as a hypersonic missile, and the long-range Khorramshahr. Iran has repeatedly presented its underground military facilities as a way to protect its weapons and production capabilities from air strikes.

Article Title: 'Uttar Pradesh's first CM was also from Uttarakhand': Yogi hits back at Akhilesh over 'infiltrators' remark
Article Text:
Yogi Adityanath hits b​ack at Akhilesh Yadav​

NEW DELHI: Uttar Pradesh chief minister Yogi Adityanath on Wednesday hit back at Samajwadi Party (SP) president Akhilesh Yadav over his controversial "infiltrators" remark, which the BJP alleges was aimed at the residents of Uttarakhand.Adityanath, who was born in Pauri Garhwal, now part of the hill state, said Akhilesh Yadav's comment reflected a "narrow and divisive" mindset. Uttarakhand was carved out of Uttar Pradesh in 2000."Uttar Pradesh's first chief minister was also from Uttarakhand," PTI quoted Adityanath as saying at the Uttarakhand Mahotsav in Lucknow. He was referring to Govind Ballabh Pant, who was born in Almora, now part of Uttarakhand.The chief minister cited several rivers, including the Ganga, Yamuna, Saryu, Ramganga and Rapti, which originate in Uttarakhand, to argue that making such remarks against the people of "Devbhoomi" — a reference to the hill state — reflected a narrow outlook."This is a divisive mindset," he added.Adityanath also mentioned India's first Chief of Defence Staff, General Bipin Rawat, and former CDS General Anil Chauhan, both of whom hail from Uttarakhand.He also highlighted that National Security Adviser Ajit Doval was born in the hill state. He further stated that almost every family in Uttarakhand has a member serving in the armed forces.Akhilesh Yadav, a former Uttar Pradesh chief minister and Adityanath's principal political rival, had alleged on October 24 that the BJP was presenting "fabricated figures" on infiltrators.He had also claimed that Uttar Pradesh had infiltrators and described Adityanath as an "ideological infiltrator," adding that he should be sent back to Uttarakhand.
Article Summary: Yogi Adityanath hits back at Akhilesh Yadav over his controversial "infiltrators" remark. The BJP alleges the remark was aimed at the residents of Uttarakhand. AdITYanath was born in Pauri Garhwal, now part of the hill state.

Article Title: ‘I am safe, receiving treatment’: President’s bodyguard Saurabh Tomar after being shot in UP
Article Text:
The 28-year-old soldier, who is part of the mounted unit stationed at Rashtrapati Bhavan in New Delhi, was visiting his native village, Gopalpur Khadana, when the incident took place.

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Army jawan Saurabh Tomar, serving in the President’s Bodyguard (PBG) regiment, has said he is safe and undergoing treatment in Meerut after being shot in the head allegedly by two neighbours in Uttar Pradesh ’s Baghpat on Diwali night.Speaking to ANI, Saurabh said, “I am serving in the President’s Bodyguard. A man named Dheeraj, who belongs to my village, shot me. I have lodged a complaint at the local police station, and the police have responded. I am currently receiving medical treatment in Meerut, and I am safe.”The 28-year-old soldier, who is part of the mounted unit stationed at Rashtrapati Bhavan in New Delhi, was visiting his native village, Gopalpur Khadana, when the incident took place. He and his brother Vineet were standing outside their house when two neighbours, identified as Dheeraj and Monu alias Praveen, allegedly confronted them over an old rivalry.According to his brother Vineet, the family was sitting outside their home when the accused arrived and got into an argument with them. One of the men allegedly pulled out a country-made weapon and shot Saurabh when he came outside. Vineet also suffered serious head injuries after being attacked with a stick.Saurabh underwent surgery at a hospital in Meerut on Monday and was declared out of danger. Police have registered an attempt-to-murder case against the two accused, who remain at large.Baraut Circle CO Anshu Jain said police received information around 10pm on November 8 that two individuals, Sonu and Dheeraj, had shot and injured a local resident in Gopalpur Khadana village.President’s Bodyguard is the Indian Army’s senior-most regiment in the order of precedence. Based at Rashtrapati Bhavan, the cavalry unit performs ceremonial escort and security duties for President of India. Its personnel participate in mounted ceremonial displays and are also equipped with armoured vehicles for operational deployment.
Article Summary: Army jawan Saurabh Tomar, serving in the President’s Bodyguard (PBG) regiment, has said he is safe and undergoing treatment in Meerut. He was shot in the head allegedly by two neighbours in Uttar Pradesh ’s Baghpat on Diwali night. The 28-year-old soldier is part of the mounted unit stationed at Rashtrapati Bhavan in New Delhi.

NEW DELHI: The Ladakh administration has prohibited political protests, dharnas, rallies and other forms of collective demonstrations in Leh and Kargil during the Model Code of Conduct (MCC) for the upcoming local body elections, even as climate activist Sonam Wangchuk appealed to the Centre to intervene, warning of fresh agitation over the poll schedule.In a post on X on Wednesday, Wangchuk shared a video featuring leaders from Leh and Kargil, including the local MP, appealing to President Droupadi Murmu, Prime Minister Narendra Modi, Union home minister Amit Shah and leader of opposition in Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi to intervene. The appeal comes amid growing opposition to the proposed elections and demands for political safeguards in the Union Territory.Wangchuk said talks on the restoration of democracy had broken down and alleged that the administration was moving ahead with the elections despite concerns raised by people across Ladakh. He also questioned the timing of the polls, citing harsh winter conditions, snowfall and the seasonal migration of residents."In this video the leadership of Leh & Kargil including the Member of Parliament have come together to appeal to the honorable President, PM, HM & the LOP & fellow citizens of India to please intervene before we are forced to start peaceful but intense agitations to demonstrate our pain," he wrote.The activist also questioned the delay in the judicial inquiry commission report into the September 24 incidents in Leh, saying it had been a year since the violence. He alleged that the administration was moving quickly to conduct the elections while the report and discussions on democratic restoration remained unresolved.Meanwhile, the restriction on protests was announced through an order issued by chief electoral officer Rahul Sharma on Wednesday. It prohibits political parties, candidates, workers, supporters and others from organising or participating in dharnas, protests, demonstrations, sit-ins, hunger strikes and rallies within the municipal limits of Leh and Kargil while the MCC remains in force.The order said such activities could intimidate voters, disturb public order and affect the atmosphere required for free and fair elections. It was issued under Section 282 of the Jammu and Kashmir Municipal Act, 2000, read with the Jammu and Kashmir Municipal Committee (Election) Rules, 2003. District election officers and police authorities have been directed to ensure compliance, with violations inviting action under relevant laws."No political party, candidate, worker, supporter or any other person shall organise, hold, or participate in any dharna, protest, demonstration, sit-in, hunger strike, rally or any similar form of collective political activity within the municipal limits of the Municipal Committee, Leh and the Municipal Committee, Kargil, which is likely to impact the peaceful conduct of elections during the entire period the Model Code of Conduct remains in force," the order said as quoted by news agency PTI.Polling for the Leh and Kargil municipal committees and panchayats is scheduled for November 21, while elections to the eight Ladakh Autonomous Hill Development Councils (LAHDCs) are scheduled for December 4.
Article Summary: Ladakh authorities ban political protests, dharnas, rallies and other forms of collective demonstrations in Leh and Kargil. Activist Sonam Wangchuk appeals to the Centre to intervene, warning of fresh agitation over the poll schedule. Wangchuk says talks on the restoration of democracy had broken down and administration was moving ahead with the elections.

Article Title: 'Architect of INDIA bloc': JD(U) rejects Sonia Gandhi's remarks on Nitish Kumar in memoir
Article Text:
Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

(With PTI inputs)

NEW DELHI: The Janata Dal (United) on Wednesday described party president Nitish Kumar as the “architect” of the opposition INDIA bloc, responding to Congress leader Sonia Gandhi ’s remarks about the former Bihar chief minister in her memoir.In her book, "Belonging: A Journey of Love," released in India on Tuesday, Sonia Gandhi wrote that Nitish Kumar was “looking for an opportunity to exit the INDIA bloc” and was under the BJP ’s “influence.”“JD(U) is deeply aggrieved by the way Nitish Kumar has been portrayed in Sonia Gandhi’s book in the context of the INDIA bloc. We believe Nitish Kumar is the architect and driving force behind the alliance, which is now being led by Sonia Gandhi and Rahul Gandhi,” JD(U) spokesperson Rajeev Ranjan Prasad said in a video statement.“Most regional parties were initially reluctant to include the Congress in the INDIA bloc, and Nitish Kumar had persuaded them to come together with the Congress. The first meeting of the alliance in Patna was subsequently successful,” Prasad added.The opposition alliance held two more meetings, in Bengaluru and Mumbai, respectively.Explaining Nitish Kumar’s decision to leave the INDIA bloc, Prasad argued that the then Bihar chief minister had eventually realised that the alliance would not work because of the ambitions and regional political interests of the Congress and its allies, as well as their "inability" to take on the BJP-led National Democratic Alliance (NDA).“The role of the Congress and its allies, their ambitions and regional political interests made it clear that they did not have the capacity to take on the NDA. That is why Nitish Kumar left the INDIA bloc,” he added.Nitish Kumar, who has switched political alliances several times, rejoined the NDA in January 2024, ahead of the Lok Sabha elections. He had left the alliance to join the Mahagathbandhan in August 2022.Meanwhile, another JD(U) leader, Sanjay Kumar Jha, accused Sonia Gandhi of making "petty and frivolous" remarks.“She is a senior leader. One did not expect such petty and frivolous remarks from her. But it seems to have become a trait of all senior leaders of the Congress. Just recall what (Mallikarjun) Kharge had said recently,” the Rajya Sabha MP told reporters in Patna, referring to the Congress president’s recent “baap” (father) comment about Prime Minister Narendra Modi.“The Congress should remember that the alliance came into being not because of its own goodwill but because of the credibility that our leader enjoyed,” Jha added.“Nitish Kumar has five decades of political experience behind him, starting with student activism during the Emergency, which also led to his imprisonment. He succeeded in bringing together many leaders who wanted an alliance without the Congress. It was at the instance of our leader that they relented,” the JD(U) leader asserted.Jha also noted that Nitish Kumar had hosted the first meeting of opposition leaders in Patna, but "things did not go in a manner that he would have appreciated.""Let us not forget that although our leader hosted the first meeting of opposition leaders, He was opposed to the very acronym INDIA, which rhymes with the name of the country. It was reported widely. Moreover, it became clear soon that all this talk of the opposition party was just a ploy to grab power by leaders who were more concerned about their respective dynasties than anything else," he remarked.In the 2024 Lok Sabha elections, the INDIA bloc prevented the BJP from securing a third consecutive majority, although the saffron party formed its third successive government at the Centre with the support of its NDA allies. The JD(U) and Andhra Pradesh chief minister N Chandrababu Naidu's Telugu Desam Party are among the BJP’s key allies, together accounting for 28 seats in the Lok Sabha.In November 2025, Nitish Kumar became Bihar chief minister for the 10th time after the NDA swept the state assembly elections. He became a Rajya Sabha member in April, paving the way for Samrat Choudhary to take over as Bihar’s first BJP chief minister.
Article Summary: The Janata Dal (United) on Wednesday described party president Nitish Kumar as the “architect” of the opposition INDIA bloc. The JD(U) was responding to Congress leader Sonia Gandhi’s remarks about the former Bihar chief minister in her memoir.

Article Title: ‘Blown them away with that whistle’: TVK takes swipe at Udhayanidhi over bypolls

‘That whistle blew them away’: TVK takes dig at Udhayanidhi over bypolls

NEW DELHI: Tamil Nadu minister Aadhav Arjuna launched a sharp attack on the DMK, claiming that the party had underestimated his side and was now in a weak position in the Maduranthakam constituency.Arjuna said the DMK had earlier claimed it would win 200 constituencies but was now sitting in the opposition benches.“The DMK, which said that it would win 200 constituencies, is sitting in the Opposition benches. They took us lightly. They said, ‘These people only know how to blow whistles.’ That very whistle came to us as our symbol, and we have blown them away completely with that whistle,” he said.Arjuna further claimed that the DMK was in a “pathetic position” in the constituency and questioned whether the party would even be able to retain its election deposit.“In this constituency, the DMK is in a pathetic position. Will the DMK even get its deposit back?” he said.He also targeted Tamil Nadu leader of opposition Udhayanidhi Stalin , alleging that his remarks were damaging the DMK.“Everything that comes out of the mouth of Udhayanidhi is only obscenity. No one else needs to come to destroy the DMK; MK Stalin’s son is enough. Udhayanidhi Stalin has come to destroy the DMK,” Arjuna said.Bypolls to the Maduranthakam Assembly constituency in Chengelpet district, adjoining Chennai, and the Dharapuram constituency in Tiruppur district of western Tamil Nadu will be held on October 6.The bypolls were necessitated after AIADMK legislators Maragatham Kumaravel and P Sathyabama resigned from their posts and joined the ruling TVK. The party has fielded both of them from the same constituencies they represented after being elected in the April Assembly election.This is the first time the TVK government is facing Assembly bypolls since it assumed office in May 2026.The Left parties, which extend outside support to the TVK government and help it retain its majority, have not joined the ruling party-led alliance. Instead, they are contesting the bypolls as a separate front.Candidates of the main opposition DMK, the AIADMK and the Tamil nationalist Naam Tamilar Katchi (NTK) are also in the fray.The Vanniyar-dominated PMK, which has considerable influence in several northern parts of the state, has not extended support to any party.A key opposition campaign plank is that the bypolls were not a natural outcome but were forced on voters after the TVK “lured AIADMK MLAs” to strengthen its numbers in the Assembly.AIADMK chief Edappadi K Palaniswami has already begun campaigning, seeking “justice” over what he has described as the betrayal.

Article Title: 'Haldi was today, now preparing for cremation': Bengaluru techie out to deliver last wedding invite dies with cousin as truck runs over scooter
Article Text:
Sindhushree, a software professional, died in a tragic accident alongside her 19-year-old cousin Vidya

(With agency inputs)





BENGALURU: A day before her wedding rituals were to begin, a 27-year-old software professional was killed along with her 19-year-old cousin after a truck ran over their scooter near Deepanjalinagar Metro station on Mysuru Road on Wednesday afternoon.Sindhushree was on her way to distribute the last of her wedding invitations when the accident occurred.The tragedy turned what was supposed to be a day of wedding celebrations into one of mourning for the family. Sindhushree's haldi and Bale Shastra ceremonies were scheduled for Thursday, while her wedding reception was fixed for Sunday, November 15. Her wedding was to take place in Nagamangala taluk of Mandya district on November 16.At Victoria Hospital mortuary on Thursday, her father, Nanjundappa, an autorickshaw driver, broke down while speaking about his only daughter."My daughter was supposed to celebrate her haldi ceremony today. Instead, I am preparing to cremate her. Her wedding reception was scheduled for Sunday, and our entire house was filled with wedding preparations. Everything is over now," he said to news agency IANS.Sindhushree, who worked at a software company, had stepped out to deliver one last wedding invitation to a relative.She was riding a two-wheeler borrowed from a neighbour, with her cousin Vidya, her aunt's daughter, riding pillion.According to police, a Rajasthan-registered truck travelling towards Mysuru hit the scooter from behind around 3.30pm. The impact threw both women onto the road, after which the truck ran over them. They died on the spot.The family said Vidya was also a student and had completed her pre-university course. Her death has compounded the grief of relatives, who were preparing to celebrate the wedding.Relatives questioned the movement of heavy goods vehicles in the locality and demanded accountability for the accident. They alleged that restrictions on such vehicles could have prevented the tragedy.The truck driver fled after the accident, abandoning the vehicle. Byatarayanapura traffic police seized the truck and registered a case based on a complaint filed by Sindhushree's father.The bodies were shifted to Victoria Hospital mortuary for postmortem. Police said they would examine CCTV footage from the surrounding areas and collect expert reports as part of the investigation."We will collect the report from experts and examine CCTV footage from surrounding areas," a senior police officer said.The family, which had spent days preparing for Sindhushree's wedding, is now left to deal with the loss of two young women.
Article Summary: Sindhushree was on her way to distribute the last of her wedding invitations when the accident occurred. The tragedy turned what was supposed to be a day of wedding celebrations into one of mourning for the family. Her wedding was to take place in Nagamangala taluk of Mandya district on November 16.

Chinese President Xi Jinping on Thursday reiterated Beijing's commitment to bringing Taiwan under its control, saying the "complete reunification of the motherland" must be achieved, news agency Reuters reported.Addressing an event in Beijing marking the 160th birth anniversary of Chinese revolutionary Sun Yat-sen, Xi described resolving the Taiwan issue as an "unwavering historical mission" of the Communist Party of China, news agency Reuters reported."We will never leave any room for Taiwan independence separatist activities in any form," Xi said.He also said Beijing would take into account the situation in Taiwan and the interests of its people while pursuing reunification."We will fully consider the realities in Taiwan and fully take into account the interests and feelings of Taiwan compatriots," he said."The tide of history cannot be stopped, complete reunification of the motherland must be realised," Xi added.Sun Yat-sen, whose 160th birth anniversary is being marked this year, died in 1925.
